recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is and do not restore UserSession. Any future cleanup of stale auxiliary category or translation data should be handled as a separate, broader cleanup rather than as this already-applied removal issue.
issue_request: FHIR-19003 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I change request to remove the UserSession resource because the project that motivated it no longer used it and the resource was controversial.
initial_application: Commit cf5b106ba409c0b59c183ee25c117bba03209da3 applied the issue by deleting source/usersession and the R4 generated model class, removing UserSession from source/fhir.ini, compartments, hierarchy, and resource-list inputs, and changing release-history links to plain historical text.
additional_context: Current build scope is governed by source/fhir.ini. UserSession is absent from active resource and infrastructure-resource entries, source/usersession is absent, and the current resource-list, hierarchy, and compartment inputs contain no UserSession entry. Remaining mentions are historical release notes, an auxiliary translation table that also retains other removed resource names, and a publish.ini category entry that cannot create a current resource without fhir.ini/source registration. Zulip confirms GF#19003 was approved and that the branch build showed UserSession gone; Confluence only records earlier background that the resource might be removed.
reconciliation: No source change was made because authoritative current source already removes UserSession from the build and the remaining historical/auxiliary mentions do not change current implementer-facing resource semantics.
